title: Usually 'faith' means living assent that bears love, trust, obedience
source_text: III. Sed tamen Scriptura plerumque fidei nomine designat, non assensum quemlibet qui doctrinae a Deo revelatae praebetur, sed illum solum qui hominem sic movet & afficit, ut inde nascatur amor, & fiducia in Deum, & debita praeceptis illius obedientia. Haec est illa fides quam divinae litterae tantopere laudant & commendant: cui victoriam de mundo tribuunt; & cum qua salutem, vitam, & adoptionem individuo nexu cohaerere testantur. Ut quum dicit Joannes, Omnis qui credit Jesum esse Christum ex Deo natus est, & haec est victoria quae vincit mundum, fides nostra, 1 Joh. 5. v. 1. & 6. Et Christus ipse, Deus ita dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret, ut omnis qui credit in eum non pereat, sed habeat vitam aeternam. Joann. 3. v. 16. Item, Haec est voluntas ejus qui misit me, ut omnis qui videt Filium, & credit in eum, habeat vitam aeternam; & ego suscitabo eum ultimo die. Joann. 6. v. 40. Etenim non omnes qui quomodocunque Christo, & verbis ejus credunt, vitam habent aeternam, & adoptantur a Deo in filios, & victoriam de mundo reportant, sed illi soli qui debitam ex fide obedientiam Deo praestant, & fidem habent in bonis operibus efficacem.
pass_a_gloss: Yet Scripture for the most part designates by the name of faith not any assent given to doctrine revealed by God, but only that which so moves and affects a person that from it arise love, trust in God, and due obedience to his precepts. This is the faith divine letters so greatly praise and commend: to which they attribute victory over the world; and with which they testify that salvation, life, and adoption cohere by an indivisible bond. As when John says, Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God, and this is the victory that overcomes the world, our faith (1 John 5:1, 6). And Christ himself: God so loved the world that he gave his only-begotten Son, that everyone who believes in him should not perish but have eternal life (John 3:16). Likewise: This is the will of him who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him may have eternal life; and I will raise him up on the last day (John 6:40). For not all who somehow believe Christ and his words have eternal life, are adopted by God as sons, and carry off victory over the world, but only those who render God the obedience due from faith and have a faith effective in good works.
pass_b_english: Usually 'faith' means assent that yields love, trust, and obedience.
Only that faith is tied to salvation, adoption, and victory—not bare belief.

choices.why: Saving faith works; not idle assent.
